title: Closing reflections and Chamberlain's tours
summary: He is glad to be alive and active, and recalls the Roseland concert, national tours and the Rag and Roll Revue album.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Are there any other things that you'd like to add to this interview? We're almost finished here.

Well, I can't think of nothin' right now. I'm glad to be alive. And I'm still active on the bandstand. And I still love my drums. I could be working six nights a week if I want to, but I don't want to work six nights. Tuesday night is enough. That will keep me active, because that's all I know how to do, is play drums. Of course, I could find something else to do, you know, but I wouldn't be happy at that.
And I've been around some good bands, some good people, some good places. I had a lot of fun with Cathy Chamberlain. We played some good places. We even played
this place down here, at the Roseland. We played a concert there at the Roseland, 52nd Street and... I think it was the Roseland.

We played at the Roseland there. Benny Goodman came down to see us. They had two bands. They had another big band, a sixteen-piece band, but had us as an added attraction. We did shows in San Francisco and Chicago, Los Angeles, Buffalo, New York... Philadelphia at the Bijou Theatre.

But just the material wasn't right, you know. She's a nice-looking girl, nice personality, but she had the wrong material. We ended up doing this... We made an album The Rag and Roll Revue. You've seen the album, haven't you.
I have not seen that album, yet.
I've got it in there. I made a few dollars. Like I said, I have to thank the good Lord who's kept me going.
